column8: Tue 17 Nov: 3e and References, the plainest citable definition of the reverse form (Basel 2009, read in part); cite it as 2009, since the 2018 principles that replaced it were not read; its use line's one hidden interaction (fund costs beyond the fee with near-zero waiting interest) rests on the payments carrying no margin, so check after tonight's re-size.

Tue 17 Nov: store, or half a clause in 3e: Table 2's All paid in every world invites the question what would it take, which the reverse sentence answers; the 2008 failure was forward tests too mild, so never say words were the fix.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e and Table 3, three parts per promise (what breaks it, how likely, what Table 3 does about it); rule text read at the Handbook's timeline view; cite only as SYSC 20 (deleted 2021) or the PRA's current text (row 7), and its arrangements are Table 3's actions, never a new rule (CANON A34).

Tue 17 Nov: 3c-3d, defines the range's failure as a stated figure going unpaid (her credibility with co-sponsors), never a smaller gift than hoped; both texts read; one clause at most, since co-sponsors are not her creditors.

Tue 17 Nov: Table 3 or 3e, a warning time per failure; the Keel arithmetic on Table 3 dates checks (31 Mar 2028 is 2 years 9 months before 1 Jan 2031 and 4 years 9 months before the first payment); warning buys a changed plan, never a repaired one; under the density cut the times go to Table 3, not 3e's prose.

Tue 17 Nov: one clause in 3e at most, a regulator's words for card Q9c's point that the plan answers for the money, not the site or the people; read at source; Taiwan law and building risk stay outside the case.
Tue 17 Nov: a citation guard for whoever cites rows 3 or 5: SYSC 20 deleted for FCA firms from 31 Dec 2021, now the PRA Rulebook and MIFIDPRU 7; the PRA chapter 15 rule text itself was not read.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e, step 3 maps cleanly: the case's high degree of certainty is the appetite each failure condition is set against; current FCA text, read in extract; a firm's four-step process, so one clause at most.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e's limits shape, the newest and plainest two-step wording (define failure, then the events); a September 2025 consultation draft read in extract, so cite it as a draft; the clarity gain for lay readers is unproven (row 43).
Tue 17 Nov: Table 3, its Look closer or act when column is the EBA's triggering events, so 3e's reverse sentences and Table 3's triggers must name the same events; read in extract.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e, a supervisor's licence to state reverse tests in words and to name one residual plainly; the density cut already settles the form, so supporting only; read in extract.
Tue 17 Nov: store; the one text naming these tests as a communication aid, but to a board; never cite it as evidence that lay readers or judges find the form clearer (row 43).
Tue 17 Nov: store, or a References definition if 3e names the method; plain, but insolvency is a balance-sheet test and Laura's tests are payment by payment.
Tue 17 Nov: store; Table 3's Who column and the January broker-statement check already answer how and how often; adds only a regulator's name for it.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; shows the form spreading beyond banks, with the member unnamed; serves no part.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e contrast, insurers needed several severe shocks together to fail while Laura's payments fail on single non-market events; fix the use line: until 1 Jan 2027 a yield fall of about 3.6 points (3.89 at today's rates) is a single market event too (NUMBERS 5, Table 3's note), and judges read the report before that date; bulletin read at source.
Tue 17 Nov: store; fix the use line: the base case does need actions, its trades on set days in 2027, 2028 and 2031 (Table 3 row 5), so say it needs no recovery action, never no action at all.

Tue 17 Nov: store, the career risk behind Table 3 row 1; strike a market stress test cannot find it: a stress that ties her income to markets (card Q1, the joint recession test) finds the deposit risk too; the row adds only the method's name.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e beside Table 2, the forward and reverse split (Table 2 picks the shock and shows All paid, 3e picks the failure and names what it takes); new beside Q14b-017 and H9-041 is only the standard's lack of a reverse test; read in extract.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q14b-017's stress-test definition read at source; the practice note adds only that Table 2's 2006 replay is a forward stress test, not a reverse one.

Tue 17 Nov: the method behind 3e's failure lists; verifies and supersedes H5-141 at source (NRC PDF, extract); a source only: in prose say the smallest set of events that breaks a promise, no engineering vocabulary, as SKELETON 3e has it for defence in depth.

Tue 17 Nov: store; size the missed deposit on the plan's own standard, $57,455 short if cash waiting earns nothing, with $3,016 at today's rates beside it as Table 3 row 1 does (AHA register 5b: never $3,016 alone); the plan does not size a default, card Q4c gives only its likelihood.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e, the success-set sentence may be the plainest form; use Table 3 note's 3.60 points (about 3.6), the plan's own zero-interest figure, not nearly 4 (3.89 is the ladder at today's rates); its fund-cost clause rests on the payments carrying no margin, so check after tonight's re-size.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of row 21's one-component cut sets; IEC 61025 read on a preview page only.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e, why the default is named once; fix: it is the one event in both promises' lists, but strike every other event touches one promise, since fund costs beyond the fees sit in both the payments' and the stated figures' lists (rows 29-30); her flexibility is a limit, not a third tree; plain words in prose.

Tue 17 Nov: store, a source for the form only: Klein's premortem turns failure reasons into watches, so 3e and Table 3 name the same events (as row 10); reprint read in full; never say the team ran a premortem (Q91-036).
Tue 17 Nov: store only; trivia under Book 18 and close to flattery; Mitchell's 1989 paper goes in References only if the report uses it, and her affiliation never in prose.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q13-002 (the study, read at source there); its inference for readers of a report is UNVERIFIED, but the caution stands: use the reverse form only where the list has been tested.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e's first reverse sentence and Table 3 row 1; figures match NUMBERS 1, 2 and 5; fix the two-event set: any cost beyond the fee with waiting cash earning less than that cost needs (0.06% a year covers 0.1%, 0.31% covers 0.5%), not under 0.06% for every cost; supersedes H7-030's list; check after tonight's re-size; figures to Table 3, not prose.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e's second reverse sentence and 3c's condition; 3.09%, 3.92%, 6.86%, 0.5%, $15,569 and $1,162 match NUMBERS 3; stronger than Q84-040; check after tonight's re-size, since the payments' margin is bought from the 2028 deposit before the floor and the covers can fall; about 3% is central only.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c and 3e aha, sharper than Q22-039: a missed deposit means no range, never a broken one (IPS l.15 checked, Table 3 row 1); say it as a consequence, since aha row 4 is the one home of the principle; the erase line holds for stated figures only, the ten still $57,455 short at 0%.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e's proof sentence, IPS l.17 tested from the failure end; deletion test (NUMBERS 4) and Table 2's All paid checked; supersedes H7-107's reverse-stress line; in words in 3e's prose (density cut), never protected from crashes.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e, the evaluation Wharton asks for: reasons to change and ways a promise breaks are different lists, so 3e never says only two things can break the plan (CANON A34, no new rule); new beside Q3b-034; its few hundred dollars rests on the payments carrying no margin, so check after tonight's re-size.

Tue 17 Nov: for the exhibits owner, Table 3 row 4's any gap met from the extra Treasuries fails at zero interest under the standard (NUMBERS 2: sized to $0 spare); this is the gap tonight's re-size closes, so check after tonight's re-size and re-word or retire the row then.

Tue 17 Nov: Table 3, the reverse test sorts its levels (single-event sets, sets closed by an action, events in no set), matching its two reasons and look closer levels; card Q36 and the tables checked; never ended on schedule (IBTA).

Tue 17 Nov: 2.1 or 3e custody clause, figures match NUMBERS 8t; fix the branches: a broker failure can delay money at any balance, while the $87,000 above SIPC's $500,000 is at risk of loss only if the customer pool is short by more than SIPC fills (8t, Q72 row 13); supersedes Q3b-031's $589,655.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e's third sentence, a limit not a promise; 25.9%, 28.0% and 38.9% match NUMBERS 8q; about a quarter in words, Table 3 row 7 as the watch; never cushion or a reason to change; re-check after tonight's re-size, which takes the margin from the 2028 money before VT.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e, the range's condition in words; 3.09% and 0.27% are in NUMBERS 3 and 0, but check after tonight's re-size: the payments' margin is bought from the 2028 deposit first, so 3.09% can fall and more than ten times may not hold; part of the 0.27% now sits outside the ends (card Q45).
Tue 17 Nov: store only; restates NUMBERS 5 (when most cannot hold) and Q98-005; a wording limit, never in 3e's prose.

Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q54-006 and Q54-008 (escrow-backed bonds cut with the US in 2011 and 2025; nothing went unpaid); adds GFOA's no direct impacts quote, worth carrying into Q54-006; a downgrade is not a default.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of row 26's premortem-to-watch link, from a secondary manual read in extract.

Tue 17 Nov: for the lead, 3e's limits as three reverse sentences (two promises, one limit) with the default once; fix: under the density cut the sizes CANON C9 asks for go to Table 3, not prose; the payments' sentence changes after tonight's re-size, so check then; adopt only after panel 4's blind two-version read (row 43); keep the model's limits.
Tue 17 Nov: a gap, not a finding: panel 4 can read 3e's limits both ways blind; until then the reverse form's clarity gain is unproven.
